files.content:
# Work

Three projects from the last year, each told the same way: what the client asked for, what we did, what changed,
and what we would do differently next time.

---

## Harbour Bakery — ordering bread before the oven is on

**The brief.** Cafés ordered by text, phone and a shared spreadsheet, and the bakery spent its first hour every
morning sorting out what had been asked for.

**What we did.** A short order page for each café with last week's order filled in, and one printed sheet of totals
at 8pm.

**The result.** The morning hour of sorting is now about ten minutes, and the bakery has had no missed orders it
knows of since.

**What we would do differently.** Show the order page to the cafés in the first week, not the third.

---

## Northgate Library — an annual report people finished reading

**The brief.** The library's annual report ran to 48 pages, and its board said few people got past the foreword.

**What we did.** Cut it to 12 pages: one page of figures, one page of the year in pictures, and a short story from
each of the four branches, written with the staff who work there.

**The result.** The report was read aloud in part at the council meeting, and the library has asked us back for
next year's.

**What we would do differently.** Agree the page count with the board before writing, not after the first draft.

---

## Calder Joinery — a website that brings in the right enquiries

**The brief.** A family joinery got plenty of enquiries, but most were for small repairs they don't take on.

**What we did.** Rewrote the site around the three kinds of work they want — kitchens, staircases and windows —
with a price range on each, and a short form that asks what the job is before anything else.

**The result.** Fewer enquiries in total, and about twice as many that turn into a quote.

**What we would do differently.** Put the price ranges in from the start. We held them back at first, and that
was the change that made the difference.

---

*Draft by Writer. Each client has seen their section; Northgate's board still has to agree its quote.*
